name: origin-ui-timeline

frames.best_why: All five steps with dates and descriptions are visible, the first three read as complete, and no cursor covers them.

tagline: Steps stack on a thin vertical rail, filled up to the current stage.
summary: A vertical list of five numbered stages, each with a small date, a bold title, a description and a hollow circle on a connecting line. Steps up to the active one brighten, and clicking a title moves the marker.
appearance: A narrow column on a black stage holds a small uppercase label, a bold heading and five stacked entries. Each entry has a faint date, a title, a two-line grey description, and a small ring on a thin vertical line at the left; the first entries look brighter than the last two.
behaviour: Clicking a step title makes it the active stage, so that entry and all above it turn bright while the rest stay dim. The recording shifts the active step a few times and the rail fills up to the chosen point; nothing scrolls or folds.
demo_content: Order status for ORD-8821: Order placed, Payment confirmed, Shipped, Out for delivery and Delivered.
search_phrases: order tracking steps down the page
dots connected by a line with dates
order status stepper for a shop
checkout progress shown as a list
activity feed with dots and dates
use_when: You need a fixed sequence of stages with dates and a clear sense of how far along it is.
avoid_when: Only a handful of stages read well, and the click targets are plain titles with no button styling.
customise: Pass steps as item children and drive the active stage with value or defaultValue; headings, dates and copy are yours, while colours and rail sizing are classes in the file.
weight_why: A dozen styled divs and a few colour transitions; no animation loop.

a11y.note: Step titles are clickable headings with no button role or tab stop, so keyboard and screen reader users cannot change the active stage.

issues: Active and completed steps differ only slightly in brightness, so the current stage is hard to pick out.
polish_why: Neat rail with good rhythm, but state changes are faint and supporting text is low contrast.
